title: Saint Stephen (26 December)
hookLine: the first martyr the day after Christmas: the crib and the cross together

cards: December 26. The wrapping paper is in bags by the curb, there are leftovers in every container, and the tree is still lit. If you go to Mass that morning, the priest is wearing red, the color of blood.
On the first day after Christmas, the Church remembers a man who was stoned to death for his faith. From lullabies to a martyrdom in a single night. The Church put it there on purpose.

teach.b: Stephen first appears in Acts 6, in a dispute about food. The early community in Jerusalem was feeding its widows, and the Greek-speaking widows were being overlooked.
So the apostles chose seven men to serve at tables, and the first named is Stephen, full of faith and of the Holy Spirit.
In Catholic tradition, he was one of the first deacons. He also preached, with a power his opponents couldn't answer, and he was brought before the council.

In Acts 7 he retells Israel's story, from Abraham to Moses to the temple, and it ends badly. An angry crowd drags him outside the city and stones him. As the stones fall he prays: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Then, on his knees: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." Close echoes of two things Jesus says on the cross in Luke's gospel.
And Luke adds a detail that matters later: the witnesses laid their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul.

Martyr comes from the Greek for witness, and Stephen's own name, stephanos, means a crown, the wreath given to a winner. Why the day after Christmas? Because the Church refuses to let the crib stay sweet.

teach.h: LORD, LAY NOT THIS SIN TO THEIR CHARGE.
teach.b: The child in the manger grows up to be crucified, and people who follow him have sometimes paid with their lives. The crib and the cross belong in the same picture.
The carol Good King Wenceslas is set on this feast too: a king going out in the snow to help a poor man gathering fuel.

how: Catholics keep December 26 as the feast of Saint Stephen, the first martyr, with red vestments inside the Christmas octave; in some countries it is also a day of giving to the poor.

o: the saint whose feast ends the Christmas season

the apostle who baptized the first Gentiles

games.q: you're Stephen. the stones are falling and you're on your knees. what are your last words?
o: a curse on those who throw them.
a prayer that their sin not be held against them.
a demand for a fair trial.
games.why: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. he dies praying for them, echoing Jesus on the cross.

practice: Stephen's first job was making sure widows got fed, so bring to mind someone in need you could actually help: a food bank, a neighbor short on money, a person you pass on the same corner.
Then sit with his harder prayer, for the people who hurt him. If you pray, pray for someone who has wronged you; if not, simply hold them without wishing them harm.

wordCard.voice: Saint Stephen. One of the seven chosen in Jerusalem, honored by tradition as the first Christian martyr, remembered on December 26 in red. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a crown or victor's wreath; Stephen's name.

carryVoice: Your line: the crib and the cross. Christmas is still sweet, and now it's honest too. Day six hundred forty-one, done.
